chunks: And with this chain of narration, from Ibn Sinan, from Abdullah bin Miskan, from Malik al-Juhani, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far: 'We describe the master of this matter with the description that no one among the people has.' He said: 'No, by Allah, it will not be so forever, until he himself is the one who argues with you about that and invites you to it.'

key_terms.صَاحِبُ الْأَمْرِ: The Master of the Matter (referring to the Awaited Imam)
key_terms.يَحْتَجُّ عَلَيْكُمْ: He argues/proves against you (provides the definitive evidence)
key_terms.يَدْعُوكُمْ إِلَيْهِ: He invites you to it (calls you to accept the truth/attributes)

ai.seo_question: How do we know the descriptions of the Awaited Imam are correct?
ai.summary: In this narration from Al-Nu'mani's *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) refutes the common tendency to attribute unique, extraordinary characteristics to the Qa'im before his appearance. He establishes a crucial criterion for eschatological verification: the Imam himself must be the one to validate these attributes and invite the people to them, preventing premature or fabricated claims. This highlights the Shia principle of relying on the Imam's explicit testimony rather than speculative descriptions during the period of occultation.
